title: Time Clock off on release day stays off when Time Clock is turned on later
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in to production (the live app, app.shopview.com) as an Admin of the production test account, at its test location, Trucks Hill 2.
  • Shortly before the release reached production, have a new staff member for this test on production, staff member A, active, on the built-in Technician role, with Time Clock off, Billable set to Yes, enrolled at Trucks Hill 2 (written down with a screenshot of the staff record).
custom_steps:
1. Open Settings, Staff.
  2. Open staff member A's Edit Staff Member window.
  3. Switch Time Clock on.
  4. Click Save & Close.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Staff member A's row shows "No" in the Technician column.

Step 2:

  • Time Clock is off and Technician is off.

Step 3:

  • Time Clock is on and Technician stays off.

Step 4:

  • The window closes.
  • Staff member A's row still shows "No" in the Technician column.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 17 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11879 (Story 1, Technician toggle on a staff member), story SV-11884 (Story 6, Release day)

  • S6-E3: “A staff member who is deactivated, or has Time Clock off, at the moment the step runs starts with Technician off. Turning Time Clock on later does not turn Technician on (S1-R5). A seasonal technician who is deactivated on release day and reactivated later is not offered on any technician list until the shop turns Technician on for them.”
  • S1-R5: “In Edit Staff Member, turning Time Clock back on leaves Technician off; the user turns it on. In New Staff Member, turning Time Clock on pre-fills Technician from the role (S1-R3), unless the user has already switched Technician by hand.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

AUTOMATION: HOLD - needs the before values taken on production shortly before the release reaches production; run on production after the release
